RUMMANI:v1p93/r6.author: al-Rummānī
RUMMANI:v1p93/r6.speaker: author
RUMMANI:v1p93/r6.claim: To taste punishment means to be punished; the metaphor is stronger because tasting is active sensory seeking, and pain is cast as a taste normally associated with pleasure.
RUMMANI:v1p93/r6.anchor: حقيقته لنعذبنهم , والاستعارة أبلغ , لأن إحساس الذائق أقوى

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p132/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p132/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p132/r4.claim: Believers value truth, bow to Qur'anic verses, pray at night, and spend for God; their concealed reward contrasts with the unequal treatment of obedient and disobedient people.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p132/r4.anchor: those who are devoid of arrogance and value the truth will profess faith in it

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p438/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p438/r7.speaker: أبي، وابن عباس، والضحاك، وابن زيد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p438/r7.claim: They interpret the nearer punishment as worldly afflictions affecting people and their property.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p438/r7.anchor: والعذاب الأدنى، قال أبي، وابن عباس، والضحاك، وابن زيد: مصائب الدنيا في الأنفس والأموال.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p438/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p438/r8.speaker: ابن مسعود، والحسن بن علي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p438/r8.claim: They identify the nearer punishment as death by the sword, as at Badr.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p438/r8.anchor: وقال ابن مسعود، والحسن بن علي: هو القتل بالسيف، نحو يوم بدر.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p438/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p438/r9.speaker: مجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p438/r9.claim: Mujāhid says the nearer punishment was killing and famine inflicted on Quraysh.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p438/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p438/r10.speaker: مجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p438/r10.claim: Mujāhid also gives the grave punishment as an interpretation of the nearer punishment.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p438/r10.anchor: وقال مجاهد: القتل والجوع لقريش، وعنه: إنه عذاب القبر.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p438/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p438/r11.speaker: النخعي، ومقاتل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p438/r11.claim: Al-Nakhaʿī and Muqātil identify it as the years of famine God imposed on them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p438/r11.anchor: وقال النخعي، ومقاتل: هو السنون التي أجاعهم الله فيها.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p438/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p438/r12.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p438/r12.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās also interprets the nearer punishment as the prescribed legal penalties.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p438/r12.anchor: وقال ابن عباس أيضا: هو الحدود.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p438/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p438/r13.speaker: أبي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p438/r13.claim: Ubayy also identifies it with the violent strike, al-lizām, and the smoke.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p438/r13.anchor: وقال أبي أيضا: هو البطشة واللزام والدخان.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p438/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p438/r14.speaker: ابن عطية، التحرير، وأكثرهم
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p438/r14.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says the greater punishment is undisputedly the Hereafter; al-Taḥrīr and most commentators specify the Fire on Resurrection Day.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p438/r14.anchor: والعذاب الأكبر، قال ابن عطية: لا خلاف أنه عذاب الآخرة. وفي التحرير وأكثرهم على أن العذاب الأكبر عذاب يوم القيامة في النار.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p438/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p438/r15.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p438/r15.claim: Another view identifies the greater punishment as killing, captivity, and enslavement.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p438/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p438/r16.speaker: جعفر بن محمد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p438/r16.claim: Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad identifies the greater punishment as the Mahdī’s emergence with the sword.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p438/r16.anchor: وعن جعفر بن محمد: أنه خروج المهدي بالسيف.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p438/r17.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p438/r17.speaker: ابن مسعود
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p438/r17.claim: Ibn Masʿūd explains “so that they may return” as meaning those still alive may repent.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p438/r17.anchor: لعلهم يرجعون، قال ابن مسعود: لعل من بقي منهم يتوب.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p438/r18.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p438/r18.speaker: أبو العالية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p438/r18.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya says the phrase means that they may repent.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p438/r19.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p438/r19.speaker: مقاتل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p438/r19.claim: Muqātil says it means turning from unbelief to faith.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p438/r19.anchor: وقال مقاتل: يرجعون عن الكفر إلى الإيمان.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p438/r20.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p438/r20.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p438/r20.claim: An unnamed interpretation takes the phrase as their wishing and asking to be returned, echoing the plea “return us so we may do right.”
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p438/r20.anchor: وقيل: لعلهم يريدون الرجوع ويطلبونه لقوله: فارجعنا نعمل صالحا.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p438/r21.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p438/r21.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p438/r21.claim: Abū Ḥayyān says an intended act can be named by the act itself: wishing to return is called return, just as intending to rise for prayer is called rising.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p438/r21.anchor: وسميت إرادة الرجوع رجوعا، كما سميت إرادة القيام قياما في قوله تعالى: إذا قمتم إلى الصلاة فاغسلوا .

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p438/r22.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p438/r22.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p438/r22.claim: Although “nearer” contrasts with farther and “greater” with smaller, the nearer punishment entails lesser severity because it ends at death; the greater entails remoteness in the Hereafter, where threat must stress magnitude and severity.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p438/r22.anchor: والأكبر يتضمن الأبعد، لأنه واقع في الآخرة، والتخويف بالبعيد إنما يصلح بذكر عظمه وشدته،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p439/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p439/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p439/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī distinguishes God’s will for His own acts, which necessarily occur, from willing that servants freely choose an act while knowing they will not; the latter does not imply inability.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p439/r1.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: فإن قلت: من أين صح تفسير الرجوع بالتوبة؟

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p439/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p439/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p439/r2.claim: He compares this to a person wishing a servant would obey even though the servant’s choice is outside that person’s power.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p439/r2.anchor: كما لا يقدح في اقتدارك إرادتك أن يختار عبدك طاعتك، وهو لا يختارها، لأن اختياره لا يتعلق بقدرتك،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p439/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p439/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p439/r3.claim: Abū Ḥayyān rejects this account as Muʿtazilī doctrine, noting that Sunnis have refuted it in theology.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v8p439/r3.anchor: وهو على مذهب المعتزلة، وقد رد عليهم أهل السنة، وذلك مقرر في علم الكلام.

STUDYQURAN:32:intro/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:32:intro/r1.speaker: author

STUDYQURAN:32:intro/r14.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:32:intro/r14.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:32:intro/r14.claim: The second half contrasts people who prostrate before God's signs with those who turn away, then presents Israel as guided while following God's signs.
STUDYQURAN:32:intro/r14.anchor: The second half provides an eloquent contrast between those who prostrate before God in beholding His signs

RAZI-FULL:v25p160/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p160/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p160/r1.claim: The lower torment is worldly punishment before the afterlife: earthly punishment cannot be both extremely severe and prolonged, since severity kills and ends it, while prolonged punishment is less severe; afterlife punishment is severe and enduring.
RAZI-FULL:v25p160/r1.anchor: قبل عذاب الآخرة نذيقهم عذاب الدنيا فإن عذاب الدنيا لا نسبة له إلى عذاب الآخرة

RAZI-FULL:v25p160/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p160/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p160/r2.claim: Worldly punishment has the qualities of nearness and smallness, while afterlife punishment is distant and immense; nearness best warns about worldly punishment, but greatness best warns about afterlife punishment.
RAZI-FULL:v25p160/r2.anchor: لكن القرب في عذاب الدنيا هو الذي يصلح

RAZI-FULL:v25p160/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p160/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p160/r3.claim: An immediate mild punishment can deter more than a severe delayed one, just as some people prefer immediate reward to great reward later; calling worldly torment small would understate its threat, and calling the afterlife torment distant would weaken its warning.
RAZI-FULL:v25p160/r3.anchor: العذاب العاجل وإن كان قليلا قد يحترز منه بعض الناس أكثر مما يحترز من العذاب الشديد إذا كان آجلا

RAZI-FULL:v25p160#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p160#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p160#2/r1.claim: Razi gives two initial explanations for hope language about God: He makes them taste punishment as one who hopes does, gradually, or He punishes in a way that people might say will perhaps make them return.
RAZI-FULL:v25p160#2/r1.anchor: لعل هذه الترجى والله تعالى محال ذلك عليه فما الحكمة فيه

RAZI-FULL:v25p160#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p160#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p160#2/r2.claim: Razi's further account allows an act to be described as aiming hopefully at an outcome when the act itself does not make that outcome certain, even if certainty comes from outside it.
RAZI-FULL:v25p160#2/r2.anchor: كل فعل يتلوه أمر مطلوب من ذلك الفعل يصح تعليل ذلك الفعل بذلك الأمر

RAZI-FULL:v25p160#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p160#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p160#2/r3.claim: A trader may hope for profit despite certainty based on outside knowledge, but one cannot say a person cuts an enemy's throat hoping he dies, since that act itself entails death; Razi distinguishes certainty grounded in the act from external certainty.
RAZI-FULL:v25p160#2/r3.anchor: فإنه يصح أن يقال يفعل كذا رجاء كذا

RAZI-FULL:v25p160#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v25p160#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v25p160#2/r4.claim: Abraham's hope that God forgive him and the command to hope for the Last Day show that hope language can apply despite certainty; torment does not itself guarantee repentance, so God's knowing the outcome does not bar genuine hope language.
RAZI-FULL:v25p160#2/r4.anchor: مع أنه كان عالما بالمغفرة لكن لما لم يكن الجزم حاصلا من نفس الفعل أطلق عليه الطمع

STUDYQURAN:32:21/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:32:21/r1.speaker: IK, JJ
STUDYQURAN:32:21/r1.claim: The lesser punishment is punishment in this worldly life.
STUDYQURAN:32:21/r1.anchor: The lesser punishment is punishment in this world (IK, JJ)

STUDYQURAN:32:21/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:32:21/r2.speaker: JJ
STUDYQURAN:32:21/r2.claim: Worldly punishment can take the form of defeat and humiliation, illness, natural disaster, or other afflictions.
STUDYQURAN:32:21/r2.anchor: through the humiliation of defeat, through illness, or by natural disaster (JJ)

STUDYQURAN:32:21/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:32:21/r3.speaker: IK
STUDYQURAN:32:21/r3.claim: Others identify the lesser punishment as legal penalties against disbelievers in this world or punishment in the grave before the eternal punishment.
STUDYQURAN:32:21/r3.anchor: Others say it refers to the legal punishments brought against the disbelievers in this world or to the punishment in the grave

STUDYQURAN:32:21/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:32:21/r4.speaker: JJ
STUDYQURAN:32:21/r4.claim: The greater punishment is the punishment of the Hereafter.
STUDYQURAN:32:21/r4.anchor: The greater punishment is that of the Hereafter (JJ)

STUDYQURAN:32:21/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:32:21/r5.speaker: JJ
STUDYQURAN:32:21/r5.claim: The lesser affliction can be a mercy if it prompts reflection and return to belief, the human being's natural state.
STUDYQURAN:32:21/r5.anchor: they are afflicted with the lesser punishment as a mercy from God, as it might make them reflect and thus turn back to belief

BURSEVI:v7p93#3/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p93#3/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p93#3/r1.claim: The direct addressees are the people of Mecca.

BURSEVI:v7p93#3/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p93#3/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p93#3/r2.claim: The nearer punishment is worldly affliction: a seven-year famine after the Prophet prayed against them, starvation, smoke-like vision, other calamities, and finally killing or capture at Badr.
BURSEVI:v7p93#3/r2.anchor: عذاب الدنيا وهو ما محنوا به من القحط سبع سنين بدعاء النبي

BURSEVI:v7p93#3/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p93#3/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p93#3/r3.claim: Here dun means before the greater punishment, which is punishment in the afterlife.
BURSEVI:v7p93#3/r3.anchor: قبل العذاب الأكبر الذي هو عذاب الآخرة فدون هنا بمعنى قبل

BURSEVI:v7p93#3/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p93#3/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p93#3/r4.claim: Adna originally describes the lower place of a thing; dun likewise denotes a slightly lower position and is extended to differences in wealth and rank.
BURSEVI:v7p93#3/r4.anchor: فيقال هذا دون ذلك إذا كان أحط منه قليلا ثم استعير منه للتفاوت

BURSEVI:v7p93#3/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p93#3/r5.speaker: كشف الأسرار والكاشفي
BURSEVI:v7p93#3/r5.claim: Kashf al-asrar, followed by Kashifi, glosses the greater punishment as the eternal fire, relative to which the worldly punishment is lower.
BURSEVI:v7p93#3/r5.anchor: وتبعه الكاشفي في تفسيره (فروتر از عذاب بزركتركه خلودست در آتش)

BURSEVI:v7p93#3/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p93#3/r6.speaker: تفسير نقاش
BURSEVI:v7p93#3/r6.claim: A report from Naqqash's commentary identifies the lesser punishment as inflation and the greater as the Mahdi's appearance with a sharp sword.
BURSEVI:v7p93#3/r6.anchor: والرتب درلباب ازتفسير نقاش نقل كرده كه ادنى غلاى اسعارست واكبر خروج مهدي

BURSEVI:v7p93#3/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p93#3/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p93#3/r7.claim: Other interpretations pair worldly humiliation with the Hereafter's misery, or falling into sin with distance from God's nearness.
BURSEVI:v7p93#3/r7.anchor: وكفته اندخوارى دنيا ونكو نسارىء عقبا يا افتادن دركناه ودور افتادن ازدركاه قرب الله

BURSEVI:v7p93#3/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p93#3/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p93#3/r8.claim: The Persian couplet presents separation from union with God as a greater punishment than every burning fire.
BURSEVI:v7p93#3/r8.anchor: دور ماندن از وصال او عذاب اكبر است آتش سوز فراق ازهر عذابى بدترست

BURSEVI:v7p93#3/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p93#3/r9.speaker: حقائق البقلي
BURSEVI:v7p93#3/r9.claim: In Haqa'iq al-Buqli, the lesser punishment is deprivation of gnosis and the greater is veiling from witnessing the Known.
BURSEVI:v7p93#3/r9.anchor: وفي "حقائق البقلى" : العذاب الأدنى حرمان المعرفة والعذاب الأكبر الاحتجاب عن مشاهدة المعروف

BURSEVI:v7p93#3/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p93#3/r10.speaker: أبو الحسن الوراق
BURSEVI:v7p93#3/r10.claim: Al-Warraq calls attachment to worldly life the lesser punishment and its resulting chastisement the greater.
BURSEVI:v7p93#3/r10.anchor: وقال أبو الحسن الوراق : الأدنى الحرص على الدنيا والأكبر العذاب عليه

BURSEVI:v7p93#3/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p93#3/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p93#3/r11.claim: La'all means that those who remain and witness the punishment may return; it can also mean kay, expressing purpose: that they repent of disbelief and sins.
BURSEVI:v7p93#3/r11.anchor: أي : لعل من بقي منهم وشاهده ولعل من مثله بمعنى كي {يرجعون} ويتوبون عن الكفر

BURSEVI:v7p93#3/r12.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p93#3/r12.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v7p93#3/r12.claim: For seekers, a pause from spiritual travel caused by self-admiration, weariness, imagined acceptance, or worldly distraction may bring affliction to awaken them from heedlessness and restore sincere seeking and love.
BURSEVI:v7p93#3/r12.anchor: يشير إلى أرباب الطلب وأصحاب السلوك إذا وقعت لأحدهم في أثناء السلوك وقفة لعجب تداخله أو لملالة

BURSEVI:v7p93#3/r13.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p93#3/r13.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v7p93#3/r13.claim: Trials of self, property, home, family, and loved ones can prompt recovery before the greater spiritual punishment of abandonment, estrangement, and a hardened heart.
BURSEVI:v7p93#3/r13.anchor: ابتلاه الله إما ببلاء في نفسه أو ماله أو بيته من أهاليه وأقربائه وأحبائه لعلهم بإذاقة عذاب البلاء

BURSEVI:v7p94/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v7p94/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v7p94/r4.claim: The Sufi reading links return to the verse about hearts being turned, and takes the aim to be renewed sincerity in seeking and height of love.
BURSEVI:v7p94/r4.anchor: لعلهم يرجعون إلى صدق طلبهم وعلو محبتهم

TAB-FULL:v18p627/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p627/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v18p627/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies the lesser torment as worldly calamities, sickness, and trials by which God afflicts people until they repent; another report from him calls it worldly trial and calamities.
TAB-FULL:v18p627/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس، " {ولنذيقنهم من العذاب الأدنى} [السجدة: 21] يقول: مصائب الدنيا وأسقامها وبلاؤها مما يبتلي الله بها العباد حتى يتوبوا

TAB-FULL:v18p627/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p627/r2.speaker: أبي بن كعب
TAB-FULL:v18p627/r2.claim: Ubayy b. Kaʿb calls it worldly misfortunes and names the smoke, the seizure, and al-lizām as events that had already occurred; a fuller chain varies over seizure or smoke.
TAB-FULL:v18p627/r2.anchor: عن أبي بن كعب، " {ولنذيقنهم من العذاب الأدنى} [السجدة: 21] قال: المصيبات في الدنيا

TAB-FULL:v18p627/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p627/r3.speaker: أبو موسى
TAB-FULL:v18p627/r3.claim: Abū Mūsā notes that Yaḥyā b. Saʿīd’s first transmission from Ubayy omits Yaḥyā b. al-Jazzār, leaving out one narrator.
TAB-FULL:v18p627/r3.anchor: قال أبو موسى: ترك يحيى بن سعيد يحيى بن الجزار، نقصان رجل

TAB-FULL:v18p628/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p628/r1.speaker: أبو العالية
TAB-FULL:v18p628/r1.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya glosses the lesser torment as worldly afflictions.
TAB-FULL:v18p628/r1.anchor: عن أبي العالية، " {ولنذيقنهم من العذاب الأدنى} [السجدة: 21] قال: المصائب في الدنيا

TAB-FULL:v18p628/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p628/r2.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v18p628/r2.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk says it means calamities in people’s worldly lives and property.
TAB-FULL:v18p628/r2.anchor: عن الضحاك، " {ولنذيقنهم من العذاب الأدنى دون العذاب الأكبر} [السجدة: 21] قال: المصيبات في دنياهم وأموالهم

TAB-FULL:v18p628/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p628/r3.speaker: الحسن
TAB-FULL:v18p628/r3.claim: Al-Ḥasan says it means calamities of this world.
TAB-FULL:v18p628/r3.anchor: عن قتادة، حدثه عن الحسن: قوله " {ولنذيقنهم من العذاب الأدنى} [السجدة: 21] أي: مصيبات الدنيا

TAB-FULL:v18p628/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p628/r4.speaker: إبراهيم
TAB-FULL:v18p628/r4.claim: Ibrāhīm says it means things people suffer in this world.
TAB-FULL:v18p628/r4.anchor: عن إبراهيم، " {ولنذيقنهم من العذاب الأدنى} [السجدة: 21] قال: أشياء يصابون بها في الدنيا

TAB-FULL:v18p628/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p628/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v18p628/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās also interprets the lesser torment as legal punishments.
TAB-FULL:v18p628/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس، " {ولنذيقنهم من العذاب الأدنى دون العذاب الأكبر} [السجدة: 21] قال: الحدود

TAB-FULL:v18p628/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p628/r6.speaker: عبد الله
TAB-FULL:v18p628/r6.claim: ʿAbd Allāh identifies it as the sword’s killing at Badr.
TAB-FULL:v18p628/r6.anchor: عن عبد الله، " {ولنذيقنهم من العذاب الأدنى} [السجدة: 21] قال: يوم بدر

TAB-FULL:v18p628/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p628/r7.speaker: الحسن بن علي
TAB-FULL:v18p628/r7.claim: Al-Ḥasan b. ʿAlī interprets it as execution by the sword.
TAB-FULL:v18p628/r7.anchor: عن الحسن بن علي، أنه قال " {ولنذيقنهم من العذاب الأدنى دون العذاب الأكبر} [السجدة: 21] قال: القتل بالسيف صبرا

TAB-FULL:v18p628/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p628/r8.speaker: عبد الله بن الحارث بن نوفل
TAB-FULL:v18p628/r8.claim: ʿAbd Allāh b. al-Ḥārith b. Nawfal says the lesser torment promised to this community is the sword.
TAB-FULL:v18p628/r8.anchor: عن عبد الله بن الحارث بن نوفل، " {ولنذيقنهم من العذاب الأدنى دون العذاب الأكبر} [السجدة: 21] قال: القتل بالسيف

TAB-FULL:v18p631/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p631/r1.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v18p631/r1.claim: Mujāhid says Quraysh were made to taste killing and hunger in this world.
TAB-FULL:v18p631/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد، " {ولنذيقنهم من العذاب الأدنى دون العذاب الأكبر} [السجدة: 21] قال: القتل والجوع لقريش في الدنيا

TAB-FULL:v18p631/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p631/r2.speaker: أبي بن كعب
TAB-FULL:v18p631/r2.claim: Qatāda transmits Mujāhid’s report from Ubayy b. Kaʿb that the lesser torment was the day of Badr.
TAB-FULL:v18p631/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، قال: كان مجاهد يحدث عن أبي بن كعب، أنه كان يقول " {ولنذيقنهم من العذاب الأدنى دون العذاب الأكبر} [السجدة: 21] يوم بدر

TAB-FULL:v18p631/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p631/r3.speaker: إبراهيم
TAB-FULL:v18p631/r3.claim: Ibrāhīm says the lesser torment was years of famine that struck them.
TAB-FULL:v18p631/r3.anchor: عن إبراهيم، " {ولنذيقنهم من العذاب الأدنى دون العذاب الأكبر} [السجدة: 21] قال: سنون أصابتهم

TAB-FULL:v18p631/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p631/r4.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v18p631/r4.claim: Mujāhid also says the lesser torment is in the graves and in worldly punishment.
TAB-FULL:v18p631/r4.anchor: عن أبي يحيى، عن مجاهد: " {ولنذيقنهم من العذاب الأدنى

TAB-FULL:v18p631/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p631/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v18p631/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd glosses the lesser torment simply as worldly punishment.
TAB-FULL:v18p631/r5.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله " {ولنذيقنهم من العذاب الأدنى} [السجدة: 21] قال: العذاب الأدنى: عذاب الدنيا

TAB-FULL:v18p631/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p631/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p631/r6.claim: Al-Ṭabarī takes the lesser torment to encompass worldly hardship generally—famine, killing, and calamities affecting people and property—rather than one exclusive kind; God inflicted all these and fulfilled His promise.
TAB-FULL:v18p631/r6.anchor: وأولى الأقوال في ذلك أن يقال: إن الله وعد هؤلاء الفسقة المكذبين بوعيده في الدنيا العذاب الأدنى

TAB-FULL:v18p633/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p633/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p633/r1.claim: The greater torment is the torment of the Day of Resurrection.
TAB-FULL:v18p633/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد، " {دون العذاب الأكبر} [السجدة: 21] يوم القيامة في الآخرة

TAB-FULL:v18p633/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p633/r2.speaker: عبد الله
TAB-FULL:v18p633/r2.claim: ʿAbd Allāh says the greater torment is the Day of Resurrection.
TAB-FULL:v18p633/r2.anchor: عن مسروق، عن عبد الله، " {دون العذاب الأكبر} [السجدة: 21] قال: يوم القيامة

TAB-FULL:v18p633/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p633/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v18p633/r3.claim: Mujāhid identifies the greater torment as the hereafter’s Judgment Day.
TAB-FULL:v18p633/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد، " {دون العذاب الأكبر} [السجدة: 21] يوم القيامة في الآخرة

TAB-FULL:v18p633/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p633/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v18p633/r4.claim: Qatāda, reporting al-Ḥasan, says the greater torment is the Day of Resurrection.
TAB-FULL:v18p633/r4.anchor: عن قتادة، " {دون العذاب الأكبر} [السجدة: 21] يوم القيامة

TAB-FULL:v18p633/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p633/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v18p633/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd says the greater torment is the punishment of the hereafter.
TAB-FULL:v18p633/r5.anchor: قال ابن زيد في قوله " {دون العذاب الأكبر} [السجدة: 21] قال: العذاب الأكبر: عذاب الآخرة

TAB-FULL:v18p634/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p634/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v18p634/r1.claim: The lesser torment is inflicted so that they may turn back and repent.

TAB-FULL:v18p634/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p634/r2.speaker: عبد الله
TAB-FULL:v18p634/r2.claim: ʿAbd Allāh glosses “so that they may return” as “they repent.”
TAB-FULL:v18p634/r2.anchor: عن عبد الله، " {لعلهم يرجعون} [السجدة: 21] قال: يتوبون

TAB-FULL:v18p634/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p634/r3.speaker: أبو العالية
TAB-FULL:v18p634/r3.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya glosses it as repentance.
TAB-FULL:v18p634/r3.anchor: عن أبي العالية: " {لعلهم يرجعون} [السجدة: 21] قال: يتوبون

TAB-FULL:v18p634/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v18p634/r4.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v18p634/r4.claim: Qatāda says they are made to return by repenting.

TABATABAI:32:19-23/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:32:19-23/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:32:19-23/r8.claim: Because the hoped-for return is repentance, the nearer punishment is worldly warning, such as famine, illness, or killing; the greater is punishment on Resurrection Day.
TABATABAI:32:19-23/r8.anchor: مثل السنين والأمراض والقتل ونحو ذلك قبل العذاب الأكبر يوم القيامة

TABATABAI:32:19-23/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:32:19-23/r9.speaker: قيل
TABATABAI:32:19-23/r9.claim: One explanation says al-adnā suits warning better than al-aṣghar, which makes punishment sound lesser, or al-ab'ad, which does not fit the threatening context.

TABATABAI:32:15-30#3/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:32:15-30#3/r6.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
TABATABAI:32:15-30#3/r6.claim: Abu Idris al-Khawlani reports that the Prophet identified the nearer punishment as worldly disasters, illnesses, and hardships for transgressors, but purification and expiation for believers.

TABATABAI:32:15-30#4/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:32:15-30#4/r1.speaker: أبو جعفر وأبو عبد الله عليهما السلام
TABATABAI:32:15-30#4/r1.claim: Al-Majma' reports from Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah that the nearer punishment is the Beast and the Dajjal.
TABATABAI:32:15-30#4/r1.anchor: في الرواية عن أبي جعفر وأبي عبد الله عليه السلام أن العذاب الأدنى الدابة والدجال

TABRISI:32:21-23/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:32:21-23/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:32:21-23/r4.claim: The greater punishment is Hell in the afterlife; the lower punishment is worldly, and authorities differ about what it is.
TABRISI:32:21-23/r4.anchor: المعنى: ثم أقسم سبحانه في هذه الآية فقال { ولنذيقنهم من العذاب الأدنى دون العذاب الأكبر } أما العذاب الأكبر

TABRISI:32:21-23/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:32:21-23/r5.speaker: أبي بن كعب وابن عباس وأبي العالية والحسن
TABRISI:32:21-23/r5.claim: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, Ibn Abbas, Abu al-Aliya, and Hasan identify the lower punishment as calamities and trials affecting people and property.
TABRISI:32:21-23/r5.anchor: فقيل: إنه المصائب والمحن في الأنفس والأموال عن أبي بن كعب وابن عباس وأبي العالية والحسن

TABRISI:32:21-23/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:32:21-23/r6.speaker: ابن مسعود وقتادة والسدي
TABRISI:32:21-23/r6.claim: Ibn Masud, Qatada, and al-Suddi identify it as being killed by the sword at Badr.
TABRISI:32:21-23/r6.anchor: وقيل: هو القتل يوم بدر بالسيف عن ابن مسعود وقتادة والسدي

TABRISI:32:21-23/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:32:21-23/r7.speaker: مقاتل
TABRISI:32:21-23/r7.claim: Muqatil says it was the seven-year famine in Mecca, when people ate carrion and dogs.
TABRISI:32:21-23/r7.anchor: وقيل: هو ما ابتلوا به من الجوع سبع سنين بمكة حتى أكلوا الجيف والكلاب عن مقاتل

TABRISI:32:21-23/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:32:21-23/r8.speaker: عكرمة وابن عباس
TABRISI:32:21-23/r8.claim: Ikrima and Ibn Abbas identify the lower punishment as prescribed legal penalties.
TABRISI:32:21-23/r8.anchor: وقيل: هو الحدود عن عكرمة وابن عباس

TABRISI:32:21-23/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:32:21-23/r9.speaker: مجاهد وأبو عبد الله
TABRISI:32:21-23/r9.claim: Mujahid identifies the lower punishment as punishment in the grave, an interpretation also reported from Abu Abd Allah.
TABRISI:32:21-23/r9.anchor: وقيل: هو عذاب القبر عن مجاهد وروي أيضا عن أبي عبد الله ع

TABRISI:32:21-23/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:32:21-23/r10.speaker: أبو جعفر وأبو عبد الله
TABRISI:32:21-23/r10.claim: The predominant report from Abu Jaʿfar and Abu Abd Allah identifies the lower punishment as the Beast and the Dajjal.
TABRISI:32:21-23/r10.anchor: والأكثر في الرواية عن أبي جعفر ع وأبي عبد الله ع إن العذاب الأدنى الدابة والدجال

TABRISI:32:21-23/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:32:21-23/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:32:21-23/r11.claim: The punishment is intended to bring them back to the truth and repentance from disbelief.
TABRISI:32:21-23/r11.anchor: لعلهم يرجعون } أي ليرجعوا إلى الحق ويتوبوا من الكفر

TABRISI:32:21-23/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:32:21-23/r12.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:32:21-23/r12.claim: Another view takes “so they may return” to mean that later people might refrain from the same sins.
TABRISI:32:21-23/r12.anchor: وقيل: ليرجع الآخرون عن أن يذنبوا مثل ذنوبهم

THALABI:v7p333/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p333/r1.speaker: أبي بن كعب وأبو العالية والضحاك والحسن وإبراهيم
THALABI:v7p333/r1.claim: These authorities say the lesser punishment is worldly illness, calamities, and trials until people repent; al-Walibi transmits this from Ibn ʿAbbas.
THALABI:v7p333/r1.anchor: قال أبي بن كعب وأبو العالية والضحاك والحسن وإبراهيم: العذاب الأدنى مصائب الدنيا وأسقامها وبلاؤها مما يبتلي الله به العباد

THALABI:v7p333/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p333/r2.speaker: عكرمة
THALABI:v7p333/r2.claim: ʿIkrima, reporting from Ibn ʿAbbas, identifies it as legal penalties.

THALABI:v7p333/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p333/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود والحسن بن علي وعبد الله بن الحرث
THALABI:v7p333/r3.claim: Ibn Masʿud, al-Hasan ibn ʿAli, and ʿAbd Allah ibn al-Harith identify it as death by the sword at Badr.
THALABI:v7p333/r3.anchor: عبد الله بن مسعود والحسن بن علي وعبد الله بن الحرث: القتل بالسيف يوم بدر

THALABI:v7p333/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p333/r4.speaker: مقاتل
THALABI:v7p333/r4.claim: Muqatil says it was seven years of famine in Mecca, when people ate carrion, bones, and dogs.
THALABI:v7p333/r4.anchor: مقاتل: الجوع سبع سنين بمكة حتى أكلوا الجيف والعظام والكلاب

THALABI:v7p333/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p333/r5.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v7p333/r5.claim: Mujahid identifies the lesser punishment as punishment in the grave.

THALABI:v7p333/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p333/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p333/r6.claim: They say the greater punishment is that of Resurrection, and the lesser is meant to turn people back from disbelief.
THALABI:v7p333/r6.anchor: قالوا: والعذاب الأكبر، يوم القيامة لعلهم يرجعون عن كفرهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p155/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p155/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p155/r1.claim: The greater punishment is the punishment of Judgment Day; the lesser punishment is what people suffer before it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p155/r1.anchor: العذاب الأكبر: هو عذاب يوم القيامة، والعذاب الأدنى هو ما يعذبون به قبل يوم القيامة.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p155/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p155/r2.speaker: ابن عباس، ابن مسعود ومجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p155/r2.claim: One view identifies the lesser punishment as the seven-year Meccan famine, during which people ate carrion; it is attributed to Ibn Abbas through Ata, Ibn Masud through Abu Ubayd, and Mujahid through Ibn Abi Najih.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p155/r2.anchor: هو الجوع الذي ابتلوا به بمكة سبع سنين حتى أكلوا الجيف. وهو قول ابن عباس في رواية عطاء، وابن مسعود

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p155/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p155/r3.speaker: أبي بن كعب، إبراهيم، الحسن ومجاهد عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p155/r3.claim: Another view makes it worldly afflictions and trials in people's wealth, intended to turn them back to God; it is attributed to Ubayy, Ibrahim, al-Hasan, and a report from Mujahid from Ibn Abbas.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p155/r3.anchor: وقال أبي بن كعب: هو مصائب الدنيا. وهو قول إبراهيم، قال: أشياء يصابون بها في الدنيا ويبتلون في أموالهم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p155/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p155/r4.speaker: عبد الله، قتادة والسدي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p155/r4.claim: A third view identifies it with the killing at Badr: Abdullah via Masruq, Qatada, and al-Suddi report the sword's punishment, which reached Qurayshi households as loss or death.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p155/r4.anchor: أن القتل يوم بدر. وهو قول عبد الله في رواية مسروق عنه، وقول قتادة والسدي، قال: العذاب الأدنى: يوم بدر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p155/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p155/r5.speaker: عبد الله بن الحارث بن نوفل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p155/r5.claim: Ibn al-Harith ibn Nawfal says that every lesser punishment God promised this community is the sword.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p155/r5.anchor: وقال عبد الله بن الحارث بن نوفل: كل شيء وعد الله هذه الأمة من العذاب الأدنى إنما هو السيف

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p155/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p155/r6.speaker: البراء ومجاهد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p155/r6.claim: A fourth view identifies the lesser punishment as the punishment of the grave, attributed to al-Bara and to Mujahid through Ibn Abi Najih.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p155/r6.anchor: القول الرابع: أن العذاب الأدنى عذاب القبر. وهو قول البراء، ومجاهد في رواية ابن أبي نجيح عنه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p155/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p155/r7.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p155/r7.claim: Although the greater punishment is otherwise agreed to be in the afterlife, Ata reports Ibn Abbas as identifying it with the killing at Badr.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v18p155/r7.anchor: وأما العذاب الأكبر فلا خلاف أنه في الآخرة، إلا ما روى عطاء عن ابن عباس أنه قال: يريد القتل يوم بدر

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:32:21-26/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:32:21-26/r1.speaker: قيل
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:32:21-26/r1.claim: One reported view identifies the lesser punishment as worldly calamities.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:32:21-26/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:32:21-26/r2.speaker: قيل
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:32:21-26/r2.claim: Another reported view identifies it as the killing at Badr.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:32:21-26/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:32:21-26/r3.speaker: قيل
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:32:21-26/r3.claim: Another reported view identifies it as the punishment of the grave.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:32:21-26/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:32:21-26/r4.speaker: قيل
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:32:21-26/r4.claim: Another reported view identifies it as seven years of famine.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:32:21-26/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:32:21-26/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:32:21-26/r5.claim: The preferred interpretation is worldly calamities together with famine, because these may lead people to return to God.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:32:21-26/r5.anchor: والأولى المصيبات والجوع لقوله: { لعلهم يرجعون }

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p692#2/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p692#2/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p692#2/r1.claim: Ibn Masʿūd identifies the lesser punishment as the day of Badr.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p692#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن مسعود قال: هو يوم بدر

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p692#2/r2.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p692#2/r2.speaker: الحسن
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p692#2/r2.claim: Al-Ḥasan says the lesser punishment was the sword at Badr.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p692#2/r2.anchor: عن الحسن، قال: العذاب الأدنى بالسيف يوم بدر

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p692#2/r3.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p692#2/r3.speaker: مجاهد
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p692#2/r3.claim: Mujāhid includes worldly punishment and punishment of the grave as lesser than the greater, harsher punishment of Hell.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p692#2/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد، قال: عذاب الدنيا وعذاب القبر دون العذاب الأكبر جهنم، والأكبر الأشد

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p692#2/r4.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p692#2/r4.speaker: السدي
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p692#2/r4.claim: Al-Suddī takes al-adnā to mean the nearer punishment, namely hunger in this world.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p692#2/r4.anchor: وقال السدي: يعني بالعذاب الأدنى: العذاب الأقرب، وهو الجوع في الدنيا

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p692#2/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p692#2/r5.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p692#2/r5.claim: The greater punishment is the fire of the Hereafter; al-adnā means nearer, as in 53:9.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p692#2/r5.anchor: {دون العذاب الأكبر} [السجدة: 21] ، يعني: النار في الآخرة، كقوله في والنجم: {فكان قاب قوسين أو أدنى} [النجم: 9] ، يعني: أقرب

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p692#2/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p692#2/r6.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p692#2/r6.claim: The phrase refers to those of them who remain.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p692#2/r7.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p692#2/r7.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p692#2/r7.claim: The purpose is that they turn from associating partners with God to faith.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p692#2/r8.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p692#2/r8.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p692#2/r8.claim: God punished them by the sword at Badr and later punished whomever He willed to bring to faith.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v2p692#2/r8.anchor: فعذبهم بالسيف يوم بدر، ومن بعدهم على من شاء الإيمان

QASHANI:32:21-23/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:32:21-23/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:32:21-23/r1.claim: The lesser punishment is the pain of consequences and fires caused by resisting the self and temperament through afflictions, hardships, and terrors; the greater punishment is veiling by darkness from the divine attributes and essence.
QASHANI:32:21-23/r1.anchor: الذي هو الاحتجاب بالظلمات عن أنوار الصفات والذات

QASHANI:32:21-23/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:32:21-23/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:32:21-23/r2.claim: The lesser punishment may return them to God by cleansing their primordial nature through hardship before dense veiling and corruption take hold.
QASHANI:32:21-23/r2.anchor: إلى الله عند تصفية فطرتهم بشدة العذاب الأدنى قبل الرين بكثافة الحجاب

ELMALILI:32:21-22/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:32:21-22/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:32:21-22/r1.claim: The nearer, lesser punishment is worldly punishment; the greater punishment is the punishment of the afterlife.
ELMALILI:32:21-22/r1.anchor: “Azâb-ı ednâ”, yakın azab dünya azabı; “azâb-ı ekber” de âhiret azâbıdır.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:32:20/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:32:20/r2.speaker: Tefsirlerde genellikle
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:32:20/r2.claim: Commentaries generally identify the greater punishment as punishment in the afterlife.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:32:20/r2.anchor: Tefsirlerde genellikle, 21. âyette geçen “büyük azap”tan maksadın âhiret azabı olduğu belirtilir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:32:20/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:32:20/r3.speaker: Tefsirlerde genellikle
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:32:20/r3.claim: Commentaries generally explain the nearer punishment as worldly calamities and hardships.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:32:20/r3.anchor: “yakın azap” ise daha çok dünya hayatındaki belâ ve sıkıntılar şeklinde açıklanır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:32:20/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:32:20/r4.speaker: Bazı müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:32:20/r4.claim: Some exegetes interpret the nearer punishment as punishment in the grave.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:32:20/r4.anchor: Bazı müfessirler bunu kabir azabı olarak yorumlamışlar

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:32:20/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:32:20/r5.speaker: İbn Mes‘ûd
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:32:20/r5.claim: A report from Ibn Masʿūd reads the verse as pointing to the polytheists’ defeat at the Battle of Badr.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:32:20/r5.anchor: İbn Mes‘ûd’dan da burada müşriklerin Bedir Savaşı’nda mağlûp olacaklarına işaret bulunduğu yorumu nakledilmiştir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:32:20/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:32:20/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:32:20/r6.claim: Because it is imposed to allow return from disbelief, the nearer punishment most likely means worldly material and spiritual distress that gives people a chance for self-examination.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:32:20/r6.anchor: dünya hayatında vicdan muhasebesi yapmalarına imkân sağlayan özellikle maddî-mânevî sıkıntılara ve bunalımlara mâruz bırakılmasının kastedildiği söylenebilir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:32:20/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:32:20/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:32:20/r7.claim: The next verse supports this reading: a person given such opportunities who remains stubborn has reached the height of injustice and definitively deserves punishment.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:32:20/r7.anchor: Müteakip âyette kendisine bu tür fırsatlar sağlandığı halde bağnaz tutumunda direnen kişinin haksızlığın zirvesine tırmanmış ve artık cezayı kesin olarak hak etmiş olduğunun belirtilmesi de bu mânayı desteklemektedir

SULAMI:v2p139/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p139/r1.speaker: أبو سليمان الداراني
SULAMI:v2p139/r1.claim: Abū Sulaymān al-Dārānī identifies the lesser punishment as abandonment and the greater punishment as eternal residence in the Fire.
SULAMI:v2p139/r1.anchor: قال أبو سليمان الداراني : ^ ( العذاب الأدنى ) ^ الخذلان والعذاب الأكبر الخلود في النيران

SULAMI:v2p139/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p139/r2.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p139/r2.claim: Another view identifies the lesser punishment as humiliation and the greater as eternal residence in the Fire.
SULAMI:v2p139/r2.anchor: وقال بعضهم : ^ ( العذاب الأدنى ) ^ : الهوان ، و ^ ( العذاب الأكبر ) ^ الخلود في النيران

SULAMI:v2p139/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p139/r3.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p139/r3.claim: A further view identifies the lesser punishment as humiliation and the greater as abandonment.
SULAMI:v2p139/r3.anchor: وقال بعضهم : العذاب الأدنى الهوان والعذاب الأكبر الخذلان

DAMGHANI:v1p175/r3.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p175/r3.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p175/r3.claim: Adnā means nearer: the lesser punishment is worldly hunger, contrasted with the greater punishment of Hell in the afterlife.
DAMGHANI:v1p175/r3.anchor: الثاني : أدنى يعني أقرب كقوله تعالى في سورة حم السجدة

DAMGHANI:v1p186/r4.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p186/r4.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p186/r4.claim: Taste can mean to punish; God made the town taste hunger and fear and will make people taste a nearer punishment.
DAMGHANI:v1p186/r4.anchor: الرابع : الذوق العذاب قوله تعالى في سورة النحل

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p119/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p119/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p119/r6.claim: Adnā can mean nearer; one alternative takes “the nearer punishment” as return.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p119/r6.anchor: والثاني : بمعنى أقرب . ومنه قوله تعالى في تنزيل السجدة :

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p119/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p119/r7.speaker: قيل
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p119/r7.claim: An alternative interpretation takes al-ʿadhāb al-adnā as a reference to returning.

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p448/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p448/r9.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p448/r9.claim: Al-ʿadhāb can mean killing; some identify the lower punishment in 32:21 with the killing at Badr.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p448/r9.anchor: والسابع : القتل . ومنه قوله تعالى في الحشر

FARRA:v2p332/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p332/r2.speaker: إبراهيم أو مجاهد
FARRA:v2p332/r2.claim: The lesser punishment means afflictions that befall people in this world, before God's punishment on the Day of Resurrection; al-Farrāʾ is unsure whether the report is from Ibrahim or Mujahid.
FARRA:v2p332/r2.anchor: عن منصور عن إبراهيم أو عن مجاهد- شك الفراء- في قوله

NAHHAS:v3p295/r9.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p295/r9.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p295/r9.claim: The lām is an oath particle.

NAHHAS:v3p295/r10.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v3p295/r10.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v3p295/r10.claim: Al-adnā means the nearer punishment; most exegetes identify it as worldly afflictions.
NAHHAS:v3p295/r10.anchor: أي الأقرب وأكثر أهل التفسير على أنها المصيبات في الدنيا

ZAJJAJ:v4p208/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p208/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v4p208/r4.claim: The lower punishment is worldly and the greater punishment belongs to the afterlife.

ZAJJAJ:v4p208/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p208/r5.speaker: قيل
ZAJJAJ:v4p208/r5.claim: One view is worldly hardship through drought and fear, supported by the verse on trials of fear, hunger, and loss.
ZAJJAJ:v4p208/r5.anchor: فقيل: ما يصيبهم من الجدب والخوف

ZAJJAJ:v4p208/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v4p208/r6.speaker: قيل
ZAJJAJ:v4p208/r6.claim: Another view identifies it as captivity and killing; generally it includes all punishment in this world.
ZAJJAJ:v4p208/r6.anchor: وجملته أن كل ما يعذب به في الدنيا

ASAD-NOTES:32:21#n16/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:32:21#n16/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:32:21#n16/r1.claim: Al-adna literally means 'nearer' and here refers to suffering in this world; Asad points to his note on 52:47.
ASAD-NOTES:32:21#n16/r1.anchor: Lit., "nearer", i:e., in this world: for an explanation, see note 27 on 52:47.

ASAD-NOTES:32:21#n17/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:32:21#n17/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:32:21#n17/r1.claim: The phrase literally means that they might return to righteousness.
ASAD-NOTES:32:21#n17/r1.anchor: Lit., "so that they might return [to righteousness]".

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p144/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p144/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p144/r3.claim: The preceding section explains why people evaded faith in the Qur'an; the succeeding verses describe believers and their reward, as well as opponents' worldly and next-world fate.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-6-2:p144/r3.anchor: The previous section of verses has outlined the reasons on account of which people were evading to profess faith in the Qur’ān.

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p110#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p110#2/r1.speaker: أبي بن كعب
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p110#2/r1.claim: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb identifies the lesser punishment as the day of Badr.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p110#2/r1.anchor: قال أبي بن كعب هو يوم بدر

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p110#2/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p110#2/r2.speaker: الحسن
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p110#2/r2.claim: Al-Hasan takes the lesser punishment to mean punishments in worldly life.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p110#2/r2.anchor: وقال الحسن العذاب الأدنى عقوبات الدنيا

ALUSI-FULL:v21p134#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p134#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p134#2/r1.claim: Al-adnā means nearer, or lesser; the worldly punishment is both nearer than the afterlife and less than its punishment.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p134#2/r1.anchor: أي الأقرب وقيل : الأقل وهو عذاب الدنيا فإنه أقرب من عذاب الآخرة وأقل منه

ALUSI-FULL:v21p134#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p134#2/r2.speaker: ابن مسعود
ALUSI-FULL:v21p134#2/r2.claim: Ibn Masʿūd identifies the lesser punishment as years of hardship that struck them; al-Ḥākim authenticates the report.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p134#2/r2.anchor: وصححه الحاكم عن إبن مسعود أنه سنون أصابتهم

ALUSI-FULL:v21p134#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p134#2/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود
ALUSI-FULL:v21p134#2/r3.claim: Ibn Masʿūd also identifies it as what befell them at Badr.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p134#2/r3.anchor: وصححه والحاكم عن إبن مسعود أيضا أنه ما أصابهم يوم بدر

ALUSI-FULL:v21p134#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p134#2/r4.speaker: الحسن بن علي
ALUSI-FULL:v21p134#2/r4.claim: Al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī similarly explains it as death by the sword, as at Badr.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p134#2/r4.anchor: نحوه عن الحسن بن علي رض يالله تعالى عنهما بلفظ هو القتل بالسيف

ALUSI-FULL:v21p134#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p134#2/r5.speaker: مجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v21p134#2/r5.claim: Mujāhid says the lesser punishment is killing and hunger.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p134#2/r5.anchor: وعن مجاهد القتل والجوع وأخرج مسلم

ALUSI-FULL:v21p134#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p134#2/r6.speaker: أبي بن كعب
ALUSI-FULL:v21p134#2/r6.claim: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb identifies it with worldly afflictions, the Romans, the seizure, and the smoke; one wording gives smoke as an alternative.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p134#2/r6.anchor: عن أبي بن كعب أنه قال : هو مصائب الدنيا والروم والبطشة والدخان

ALUSI-FULL:v21p134#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p134#2/r7.speaker: إبن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v21p134#2/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās explains it as worldly misfortunes, illnesses, and calamities.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p134#2/r7.anchor: عن إبن عباس أنه قال : هو مصائب الدنيا وأسقامها وبلاياها

ALUSI-FULL:v21p134#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p134#2/r8.speaker: إبن عباس والضحاك وإبن زيد
ALUSI-FULL:v21p134#2/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, and Ibn Zayd specify worldly afflictions affecting people and property.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p134#2/r8.anchor: عن إبن عباس أنه قال : هو مصائب الدنيا وأسقامها وبلاياها وفي رواية عنه وعن الضحاك وإبن زيد

ALUSI-FULL:v21p134#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p134#2/r9.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
ALUSI-FULL:v21p134#2/r9.claim: In a report from ʿUbāda ibn al-Ṣāmit, the Prophet calls the lesser punishment misfortunes, illnesses, and burdens that punish the profligate in this life, but are purification for believers.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p134#2/r9.anchor: سألت رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم عنها فقال عليه الصلاة والسلام : هي المصائب والأسقام والآصار

ALUSI-FULL:v21p134#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p134#2/r10.speaker: إبن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v21p134#2/r10.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās also interprets the lesser punishment as the prescribed legal penalties.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p134#2/r10.anchor: وفي رواية عن إبن عباس أنه الحدود

ALUSI-FULL:v21p134#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p134#2/r11.speaker: أبو عبيدة
ALUSI-FULL:v21p134#2/r11.claim: Abū ʿUbayda explains the lesser punishment as torment in the grave.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p134#2/r11.anchor: عن أبي عبيدة أنه فسره بعذاب القبر

ALUSI-FULL:v21p134#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p134#2/r12.speaker: مجاهد
ALUSI-FULL:v21p134#2/r12.claim: Mujāhid is also reported to have identified the lesser punishment as torment in the grave.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p134#2/r12.anchor: بعذاب القبر وحكى عن مجاهد أيضا

ALUSI-FULL:v21p134#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p134#2/r13.speaker: إبن مسعود
ALUSI-FULL:v21p134#2/r13.claim: Ibn Masʿūd and others identify the greater punishment as the punishment of the Resurrection.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p134#2/r13.anchor: هو عذاب يوم القيامة كما روى عن إبن مسعود وغيره

ALUSI-FULL:v21p134#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p134#2/r14.speaker: إبن عطية
ALUSI-FULL:v21p134#2/r14.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says there is no disagreement that the greater punishment is that of the Resurrection.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p134#2/r14.anchor: وقال : إبن عطية لا خلاف في أنه ذلك

ALUSI-FULL:v21p134#2/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p134#2/r15.speaker: التحرير
ALUSI-FULL:v21p134#2/r15.claim: Al-Taḥrīr says most interpreters understand the greater punishment as the punishment in the Fire on Resurrection Day.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p134#2/r15.anchor: وفي التحرير إن أكثرهم على أن العذاب الأكبر عذاب يوم القيامة في النار

ALUSI-FULL:v21p134#2/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p134#2/r16.speaker: قيل
ALUSI-FULL:v21p134#2/r16.claim: Another view identifies the greater punishment as killing, captivity, and imprisonment; on this reading the lesser punishment must be something milder, such as famine or illness.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p134#2/r16.anchor: وقيل : هو القتل والسبي والأسر وعن جعفر

ALUSI-FULL:v21p134#2/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p134#2/r17.speaker: جعفر بن محمد
ALUSI-FULL:v21p134#2/r17.claim: Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad identifies the greater punishment with the Mahdī's emergence with the sword.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p134#2/r17.anchor: وعن جعفر بن محمد رضي الله تعالى عنهما أنه خروج المهدي بالسيف

ALUSI-FULL:v21p134#2/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p134#2/r18.speaker: بعض أهل البيت
ALUSI-FULL:v21p134#2/r18.claim: Some members of the Prophet's family identify it with the Beast and the Antichrist; this also requires a lesser worldly punishment in contrast.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p134#2/r18.anchor: وعن بعض أهل البيت تفسيره بالدابة والدجال

ALUSI-FULL:v21p134#2/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p134#2/r19.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p134#2/r19.claim: Al-Ālūsī regards the majority interpretation, that the greater punishment is the punishment of the Hereafter, as the relied-upon view.

ALUSI-FULL:v21p135/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p135/r1.speaker: النيسابوري
ALUSI-FULL:v21p135/r1.claim: Al-Nīsābūrī, summarizing the Imām, says the wording chooses nearness rather than smallness and greatness rather than distance because proximity and greatness intensify the threat.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p135/r1.anchor: لأن المقصود هو التخويف والتهديد وذلك إنما يحصل بالقرب لا بالصغر وبالكبر لا بالبعد قاله النيسابوري

ALUSI-FULL:v21p135/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p135/r2.speaker: أبو حيان
ALUSI-FULL:v21p135/r2.claim: Abū Ḥayyān says the stated terms also imply the apparent opposites: the lesser punishment ends at death, while the greater one lies farther away in the Hereafter.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p135/r2.anchor: وكذا أبو حيان إلا أنه قال : إن الأدنى يتضمن الأصغر لأنه منقض بموت المعذب والأكبر يتضمن الأبعد

ALUSI-FULL:v21p135/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p135/r3.speaker: إبن مسعود
ALUSI-FULL:v21p135/r3.claim: Ibn Masʿūd takes the clause to mean that those who remain may repent.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p135/r3.anchor: أي لعل من بقي منهم يتوب قاله إبن مسعود

ALUSI-FULL:v21p135/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p135/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v21p135/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī allows that they may wish and ask to return to worldly life; naming the wish by its object is like calling an intention to stand standing, as in the prayer verse.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p135/r4.anchor: وقال الزمخشري : أو لعلهم يريدون الرجوع ويطلبونه

ALUSI-FULL:v21p135/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p135/r5.speaker: مجاهد وأبو عبيدة
ALUSI-FULL:v21p135/r5.claim: A reading attributed to Mujāhid and Abū ʿUbayda attaches the clause to the tasting of punishment and takes the return as a return to this world, rather than repentance.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p135/r5.anchor: حكى عن مجاهد وروى عن أبي عبيدة فيتعلق ( لعلهم ) إلخ

ALUSI-FULL:v21p135/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p135/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p135/r6.claim: A passive reading of يرجعون supports the interpretation that they hope to be returned to worldly life, since it cannot naturally mean their own repentance.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p135/r6.anchor: ووجه دلالة القراءة المذكورة عليه أنه لا يصح الحمل فيها على التوبة

ALUSI-FULL:v21p135/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p135/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v21p135/r7.claim: Al-Ālūsī prefers the transmitted explanation of repentance; the passive reading can still fit if the punishment turns them from disbelief to faith.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p135/r7.anchor: والظاهر التفسير المأثور والقراءة لا تأباه لجواز أن يكون المعنى عليها لعلهم يرجعهم ذلك العذاب عن الكفر إلى الإيمان

ALUSI-FULL:v21p135/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p135/r8.speaker: سيبويه
ALUSI-FULL:v21p135/r8.claim: Sībawayh explains لعل here as expressing hope from the addressees' perspective.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p135/r8.anchor: لترجي المخاطبين كما فسرها بذلك سيبويه

ALUSI-FULL:v21p135/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p135/r9.speaker: إبن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v21p135/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses لعل here as كي, with the sense that the punishment may expose them to repentance.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p135/r9.anchor: وعن إبن عباس تفسيرها هنا بكى وكأن المراد

ALUSI-FULL:v21p135/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v21p135/r10.speaker: الزمخشري
ALUSI-FULL:v21p135/r10.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī treats the clause as God's own hope, reinterpreted as divine willing because literal hope is impossible; al-Ālūsī dismisses his Muʿtazilī answer.
ALUSI-FULL:v21p135/r10.anchor: جعلها الزمخشري لترجيه سبحانه ولإستحالة حقيقة ذلك منه عزوجل حمله على إرادته تعالى

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p308/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p308/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p308/r1.claim: The nearer punishment means a punishment other than the greater punishment of the Hereafter.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p308/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p308/r2.speaker: أبي بن كعب، الضحاك، الحسن، إبراهيم، الوالبي عن ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p308/r2.claim: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, al-Dahhak, al-Hasan, Ibrahim, and al-Walibi from Ibn Abbas identify it as worldly calamities and illnesses.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p308/r2.anchor: قال أبي بن كعب، والضحاك، والحسن، وإبراهيم: "العذاب الأدنى" مصائب الدنيا وأسقامها،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p308/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p308/r3.speaker: عكرمة عن ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p308/r3.claim: Ikrima, transmitting from Ibn Abbas, identifies the nearer punishment as legal penalties.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p308/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p308/r4.speaker: مقاتل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p308/r4.claim: Muqatil says it was a seven-year famine in Mecca so severe that people ate carrion, bones, and dogs.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p308/r4.anchor: وقال مقاتل: الجوع سبع سنين بمكة حتى أكلوا الجيف والعظام والكلاب

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p308/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p308/r5.speaker: ابن مسعود، قتادة، السدي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p308/r5.claim: Ibn Masud, Qatada, and al-Suddi say it was death by the sword at Badr.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p308/r5.anchor: وقال ابن مسعود: هو القتل بالسيف يوم بدر (4) وهو قول قتادة والسدي،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p308/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p308/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p308/r6.claim: The worldly punishments aim to turn people back to faith; this concerns those who remained after Badr and the famine.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v6p308/r6.anchor: إلى الإيمان، يعني: من بقي منهم بعد بدر وبعد القحط.

BAYDAWI-FULL:32:21-23/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:32:21-23/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:32:21-23/r1.claim: The nearer punishment is worldly affliction: the seven-year drought, killing, and captivity they endured.
BAYDAWI-FULL:32:21-23/r1.anchor: عذاب الدنيا يريد ما محنوا به من السنة سبع سنين

BAYDAWI-FULL:32:21-23/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:32:21-23/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:32:21-23/r2.claim: The greater punishment is the punishment of the afterlife.

BAYDAWI-FULL:32:21-23/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:32:21-23/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:32:21-23/r3.claim: The hope of return concerns those who survive the worldly punishment, so that they may repent of disbelief.

BAYDAWI-FULL:32:21-23/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:32:21-23/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:32:21-23/r4.claim: A report says al-Walīd ibn ʿUqba vied with ʿAlī at Badr, and these verses were revealed.
BAYDAWI-FULL:32:21-23/r4.anchor: روي أن الوليد ابن عقبة فاخر عليا رضي الله عنه يوم بدر فنزلت هذه الآيات

BIQAI-FULL:v6p60/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p60/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p60/r7.claim: God promises all of them some punishment before the Resurrection, directly and through other agents, including punishment of the grave.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p60/r7.anchor: أي قبل يوم القيامة , بأيديكم وغيرها

BIQAI-FULL:v6p60/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p60/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p60/r8.claim: The promise answers believers’ human haste for worldly humiliation of their opponents and counters their denial of postmortem punishment and confidence in their numbers and strength.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p60/r8.anchor: بشرهم بذلك على وجه يشمل عذاب القبر

BIQAI-FULL:v6p60/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p60/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p60/r9.claim: At the sūra’s Meccan revelation, God brought Quraysh repeated drought, divided them, and caused them to be killed or captured by believers, among other punishments.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p60/r9.anchor: فأذاقهم الجدب سنين متوالية , وفرق شملهم وقتلهم وأسرهم بأيدي المؤمنين

BIQAI-FULL:v6p60/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p60/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p60/r10.claim: The greater punishment is the punishment of the Hereafter already described.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p60/r10.anchor: أي الذي مر ذكره في الآخرة

BIQAI-FULL:v6p60/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v6p60/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v6p60/r11.claim: Worldly punishment is meant to make their return from transgression conceivable; many first returned from fear of the sword, then loved Islam after seeing its virtues.
BIQAI-FULL:v6p60/r11.anchor: فلما رأوا محاسن الإسلام كانوا من أشد الناس فيه رغبة وله حبا

DURR-FULL:v6p553/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p553/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v6p553/r3.claim: Ibn Masud identifies the lesser punishment as the Battle of Badr, the greater punishment as the Day of Resurrection, and the hoped-for return as the return to faith of survivors.
DURR-FULL:v6p553/r3.anchor: عن ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه في قوله {ولنذيقنهم من العذاب الأدنى} قال: يوم بدر {دون العذاب الأكبر} قال: يوم القيامة

DURR-FULL:v6p553/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p553/r4.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v6p553/r4.claim: In another report, Ibn Masud says the lesser punishment was years of famine that struck them, so that they might repent.
DURR-FULL:v6p553/r4.anchor: عن ابن مسعود رضي الله عنه في قوله {ولنذيقنهم من العذاب الأدنى} قال: سنون اصابتهم {لعلهم يرجعون} قال: يتوبون

DURR-FULL:v6p553/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p553/r5.speaker: أبي بن كعب
DURR-FULL:v6p553/r5.claim: Ubayy ibn Ka'b lists worldly calamities, al-luzum, the violent seizure, and the smoke as forms of the lesser punishment.
DURR-FULL:v6p553/r5.anchor: عن أبي بن كعب رضي الله عنه في قوله {ولنذيقنهم من العذاب الأدنى} قال: مصائب الدنيا واللزوم والبطشة والدخان

DURR-FULL:v6p553/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p553/r6.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
DURR-FULL:v6p553/r6.claim: The Prophet identifies the lesser punishment as calamities, illnesses, and anṣāb (the source's term), a worldly chastening for the profligate; for believers it is purification and almsgiving.
DURR-FULL:v6p553/r6.anchor: سألت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم عنها فقال هي المصائب والاسقام والانصاب

DURR-FULL:v6p553/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p553/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v6p553/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas says worldly calamities, illnesses, and trials are sent so that people may repent.
DURR-FULL:v6p553/r7.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في قوله {ولنذيقنهم من العذاب الأدنى} قال: مصائب الدنيا وأسقامها وبلاياها

DURR-FULL:v6p553/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p553/r8.speaker: إبراهيم
DURR-FULL:v6p553/r8.claim: Ibrahim says the lesser punishment consists of things people suffer in this world, intended to bring them to repentance.
DURR-FULL:v6p553/r8.anchor: عن إبراهيم رضي الله عنه {ولنذيقنهم من العذاب الأدنى دون العذاب الأكبر} قال: أشياء يصابون بها في الدنيا

DURR-FULL:v6p554/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p554/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v6p554/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the lesser punishment as legal penalties and says their purpose is repentance.
DURR-FULL:v6p554/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {ولنذيقنهم من العذاب الأدنى دون العذاب الأكبر} قال: الحدود {لعلهم يرجعون} قال: يتوبون

DURR-FULL:v6p554/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p554/r2.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v6p554/r2.claim: Mujahid gives one interpretation as the punishment of worldly life and the punishment of the grave.
DURR-FULL:v6p554/r2.anchor: عن مجاهد {ولنذيقنهم من العذاب الأدنى} قال: عذاب الدنيا وعذاب القبر

DURR-FULL:v6p554/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p554/r3.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v6p554/r3.claim: In another report, Mujahid specifies killing and hunger for Quraysh in this world, with the greater punishment coming in the afterlife on Resurrection Day.
DURR-FULL:v6p554/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله {ولنذيقنهم من العذاب الأدنى} قال: القتل والجوع لقريش في الدنيا والعذاب الأكبر يوم القيامة

DURR-FULL:v6p554/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v6p554/r4.speaker: أبو عبيدة
DURR-FULL:v6p554/r4.claim: Abu Ubayda identifies the lesser punishment as punishment in the grave.
DURR-FULL:v6p554/r4.anchor: عن أبي عبيدة في قوله {ولنذيقنهم من العذاب الأدنى} قال: عذاب القبر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p363#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p363#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p363#2/r1.claim: The pronoun “them” refers to Quraysh’s unbelievers.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p363#2/r1.anchor: الضمير في قوله لنذيقنهم لكفار قريش

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p363#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p363#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p363#2/r2.claim: God will make them suffer a worldly punishment short of the afterlife’s punishment.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p363#2/r2.anchor: أعلم الله تعالى أنه يصيبهم بعذاب دون عذاب الآخرة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p363#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p363#2/r3.speaker: إبراهيم النخعي ومقاتل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p363#2/r3.claim: Ibrahim al-Nakhaʿi and Muqatil identify it as the famine years God inflicted.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p363#2/r3.anchor: فقال إبراهيم النخعي ومقاتل: هم السنون

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p363#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p363#2/r4.speaker: ابن عباس وأبي بن كعب وابن زيد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p363#2/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas, Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, and Ibn Zayd identify it as worldly afflictions such as illness.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p363#2/r4.anchor: وقال ابن عباس وأبي بن كعب: هو مصائب الدنيا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p363#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p363#2/r5.speaker: ابن مسعود والحسن بن علي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p363#2/r5.claim: Ibn Masʿud and al-Hasan ibn Ali say it is death by the sword, as at Badr and elsewhere.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p363#2/r5.anchor: وقال ابن مسعود والحسن بن علي هو القتل بالسيف

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p363#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p363#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p363#2/r6.claim: On the sword interpretation, returners are survivors different from those who tasted it, so the pronouns differ in reference.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p363#2/r6.anchor: فيكون على هذا التأويل الراجع غير الذي يذوق

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p363#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p363#2/r7.speaker: أبي بن كعب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p363#2/r7.claim: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb also identifies it with the striking, al-lizam, and smoke.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p363#2/r7.anchor: وقال أبي بن كعب أيضا هي البطشة، واللزام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p363#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p363#2/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p363#2/r8.claim: Ibn Abbas also says it refers to prescribed legal penalties.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p363#2/r8.anchor: وقال ابن عباس أيضا عنى بذلك الحدود

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p363#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p363#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p363#2/r9.claim: The legal-penalty view can apply to sinful believers.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p363#2/r9.anchor: ويتجه على هذا التأويل أن تكون في فسقة المؤمنين

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p363#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p363#2/r10.speaker: مجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p363#2/r10.claim: Mujahid identifies it as punishment in the grave.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p363#2/r10.anchor: وقال مجاهد: عنى بذلك عذاب القبر

MUSLIM:7070/r1.author: MUSLIM
MUSLIM:7070/r1.speaker: أُبَىِّ بْنِ كَعْبٍ
MUSLIM:7070/r1.claim: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb identifies the lesser punishment as worldly calamities, the Romans, and either the assault or the smoke; Shuʿba is uncertain which of those last two was meant.
MUSLIM:7070/r1.anchor: عَنْ أُبَىِّ، بْنِ كَعْبٍ فِي قَوْلِهِ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ ‏{‏ وَلَنُذِيقَنَّهُمْ مِنَ الْعَذَابِ الأَدْنَى دُونَ الْعَذَابِ الْأَكْبَرِ‏}‏ قَالَ مَصَائِبُ الدُّنْيَا وَالرُّومُ وَالْبَطْشَةُ أَوِ الدُّخَانُ

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p341#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p341#2/r1.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p341#2/r1.claim: Ibn Masud, through Masruq, identifies the nearer punishment as what befell them at Badr; Qatada and al-Suddi share this view.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p341#2/r1.anchor: أحدها أنه ما أصابهم يوم بدر رواه مسروق عن ابن مسعود وبه قال قتادة والسدي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p341#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p341#2/r2.speaker: النخعي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p341#2/r2.claim: Al-Nakha'i takes the nearer punishment as years of hardship imposed on them; Abu Ubayda transmits this view from Ibn Masud.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p341#2/r2.anchor: والثاني سنون أخذوا بها رواه أبو عبيدة عن ابن مسعود وبه قال النخعي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p341#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p341#2/r3.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p341#2/r3.claim: Muqatil specifies seven years of hunger as the affliction.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p341#2/r3.anchor: وقال مقاتل أخذوا بالجوع سبع سنين

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p341#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p341#2/r4.speaker: أبي بن كعب وابن عباس وأبو العالية والحسن وقتادة والضحاك
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p341#2/r4.claim: Ubayy ibn Ka'b, Ibn Abbas, Abu al-Aliya, al-Hasan, Qatada, and al-Dahhak identify the nearer punishment as worldly calamities.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p341#2/r4.anchor: والثالث مصائب الدنيا قاله أبي بن كعب وابن عباس في رواية ابن أبي طلحة وأبو العالية والحسن وقتادة والضحاك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p341#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p341#2/r5.speaker: عكرمة عن ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p341#2/r5.claim: Ikrima transmits from Ibn Abbas that the nearer punishment means the prescribed legal penalties.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p341#2/r5.anchor: والرابع الحدود رواه عكرمة عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p341#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p341#2/r6.speaker: البراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p341#2/r6.claim: Al-Bara identifies the nearer punishment as punishment in the grave.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p341#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p341#2/r7.speaker: مجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p341#2/r7.claim: Mujahid identifies the nearer punishment as killing and hunger.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p341#2/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p341#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p341#2/r8.claim: Dūna here means before the greater punishment.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p341#2/r8.anchor: دون العذاب الأكبر أي قبل العذاب الأكبر

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p341#2/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p341#2/r9.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p341#2/r9.claim: Ibn Masud says the greater punishment is the punishment of Judgment Day.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p341#2/r9.anchor: أحدهما أنه عذاب يوم القيامة قاله ابن مسعود

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p341#2/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p341#2/r10.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p341#2/r10.claim: Muqatil says the greater punishment is the killing at Badr.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p341#2/r10.anchor: والثاني أنه القتل ببدر قاله مقاتل

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p341#2/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p341#2/r11.speaker: أبو العالية
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p341#2/r11.claim: Abu al-Aliya understands their hoped-for return as repentance.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p341#2/r12.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p341#2/r12.speaker: ابن مسعود
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p341#2/r12.claim: Ibn Masud takes the phrase to mean that those of them who remain may repent.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p341#2/r12.anchor: وقال ابن مسعود لعل من بقي منهم يتوب

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p341#2/r13.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p341#2/r13.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p341#2/r13.claim: Muqatil understands it as a hope that they turn from disbelief to faith.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v6p341#2/r13.anchor: وقال مقاتل لكي يرجعوا عن الكفر إلى الإيمان

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p369#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p369#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p369#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas and many authorities identify the nearer punishment as worldly calamities, illness, and afflictions meant to lead people to repentance.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p369#2/r2.anchor: ابن عباس: يعني بالعذاب الأدنى مصائب الدنيا وأسقامها وآفاتها، وما يحل

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p369#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p369#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p369#2/r3.claim: In another narration, Ibn Abbas identifies the nearer punishment as carrying out legal penalties.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p369#2/r3.anchor: وقال ابن عباس -في رواية عنه -: يعني به إقامة الحدود عليهم.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p369#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p369#2/r4.speaker: البراء بن عازب ومجاهد وأبو عبيدة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p369#2/r4.claim: Al-Bara ibn Azib, Mujahid, and Abu Ubayda interpret it as punishment in the grave.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p369#2/r4.anchor: وقال البراء بن عازب، ومجاهد، وأبو عبيدة: يعني به عذاب القبر.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p369#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p369#2/r5.speaker: عبد الله
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p369#2/r5.claim: Abdullah says the nearer punishment meant drought years that struck the people; al-Nasa'i records the report without a grading here.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p369#2/r5.anchor: عن عبد الله: {ولنذيقنهم من العذاب الأدنى دون العذاب الأكبر} قال: سنون أصابتهم.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p369#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p369#2/r6.speaker: أبي بن كعب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p369#2/r6.claim: Ubayy ibn Ka'b says the nearer punishment includes calamities and the smoke that had passed, while the great assault and al-lizam remained; Muslim transmits a similar mawquf report, as does al-Bukhari from Ibn Masud.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p369#2/r6.anchor: عن أبي بن كعب في هذه الآية

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p369#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p369#2/r7.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p369#2/r7.claim: In another narration Ibn Masud says the nearer punishment was killing and captivity at Badr; Malik reports likewise from Zayd ibn Aslam.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p369#2/r7.anchor: وقال عبد الله بن مسعود (9) أيضا، في رواية عنه: العذاب الأدنى: ما أصابهم من القتل والسبي يوم بدر.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p369#2/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p369#2/r8.speaker: السدي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p369#2/r8.claim: Al-Suddi and others say every Meccan household grieved for a dead or captive relative; some faced an affliction or paid ransom, and some both.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v6p369#2/r8.anchor: قال السدي وغيره: لم يبق بيت بمكة إلا دخله الحزن على قتيل لهم أو أسير،

MUSNAD-AHMAD:21172/r1.author: Aḥmad b. Ḥanbal
MUSNAD-AHMAD:21172/r1.speaker: أبي بن كعب
MUSNAD-AHMAD:21172/r1.claim: Ubayy is reported to say that the calamities and smoke have passed, while al-batsha and al-lizām are also named in connection with the verse's punishment.
MUSNAD-AHMAD:21172/r1.anchor: عن أبي بن كعب، في هذه الآية

JISHUMI:v8p5686/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5686/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5686/r1.claim: The clause can mean that God threatens and informs them in the hope that they return; another explanation is killing and Islam’s ascendancy despite their resistance.
JISHUMI:v8p5686/r1.anchor: قلنا: معناه أوعدهم به وأخبرهم لعلهم يرجعون، وقيل: هو القتل، وظهور الإسلام على رغمهم

JISHUMI:v8p5686/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5686/r2.speaker: عبد الله، وأبو العالية، وقتادة
JISHUMI:v8p5686/r2.claim: ʿAbd Allāh, Abū al-ʿĀliya, and Qatāda explain the lower punishment as worldly punishment, meant to turn people from disbelief through repentance before the greater punishment of the afterlife.
JISHUMI:v8p5686/r2.anchor: دون العذاب الأكبر أي: عذاب الآخرة لعلهم يرجعون عن كفرهم بالتوبة، عن عبد الله، وأبي العالية، وقتادة

JISHUMI:v8p5686/r17.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v8p5686/r17.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v8p5686/r17.claim: The hope that people may return shows God wills the return of everyone, contrary to the Mujbira.
JISHUMI:v8p5686/r17.anchor: يدل قوله: (لعلهم يرجعون) أنه أراد من الجميع الرجوع، خلاف قول المجبرة

MUJAHID:v2p510#4/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p510#4/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v2p510#4/r1.claim: Mujahid identifies the nearer punishment as the killings and hunger that struck Quraysh, and the greater punishment as that of the Resurrection.
MUJAHID:v2p510#4/r1.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد ﴿ العذاب الأدنى ﴾ ما أصابهم من القتل والجوع

MUJAHID:v2p510#4/r2.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v2p510#4/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
MUJAHID:v2p510#4/r2.claim: Ibn Masʿud says the nearer punishment refers to years of famine that afflicted people before you.
MUJAHID:v2p510#4/r2.anchor: عن أبي إسحاق الهمذاني عن أبي الأحوص عن عبد الله بن مسعود في قوله ﴿ العذاب الأدنى ﴾ قال سنون أصابت قوما قبلكم

MUQATIL:32:19-21/r7.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:32:19-21/r7.speaker: author
MUQATIL:32:19-21/r7.claim: The lesser punishment was the seven-year Meccan famine, when unbelievers ate bones, dead bodies, carrion, and dogs because they rejected the Prophet.
MUQATIL:32:19-21/r7.anchor: { ولنذيقنهم } يعني كفار مكة { من العذاب الأدنى } يعني الجوع الذي أصابهم في السنين السبع بمكة

MUQATIL:32:19-21/r8.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:32:19-21/r8.speaker: author
MUQATIL:32:19-21/r8.claim: The greater punishment was killing at Badr, more severe than the famine; it was meant to bring them from unbelief back to faith.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p292#5/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p292#5/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p292#5/r1.claim: The nearer punishment is worldly punishment, including captivity and seven years of famine.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p292#5/r1.anchor: عذاب الدنيا من الاسر وما محنوا به من السنة سبع سنين

NASAFI-FULL:v3p292#5/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p292#5/r2.speaker: الضحاك
NASAFI-FULL:v3p292#5/r2.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk identifies the nearer punishment as humiliation and the greater one as abiding in the Fire.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p292#5/r2.anchor: عن الدار انى العذاب الادنى الخذلال والعذاب الأكبر الخلود فى النيران

NASAFI-FULL:v3p292#5/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p292#5/r3.speaker: قيل
NASAFI-FULL:v3p292#5/r3.claim: Another reported interpretation identifies the nearer punishment as the punishment of the grave.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p292#5/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p292#5/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p292#5/r4.claim: The aim is that those punished in this life might repent of disbelief.

QURTUBI-FULL:32:21/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:32:21/r1.speaker: الحسن وأبو العالية والضحاك وأبي بن كعب وإبراهيم النخعي وابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:32:21/r1.claim: Al-Hasan, Abu al-Aliya, al-Dahhak, Ubayy ibn Ka'b, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, and Ibn Abbas identify the lesser torment as worldly afflictions and illnesses that test people until they repent.
QURTUBI-FULL:32:21/r1.anchor: قال الحسن وأبو العالية والضحاك وأبي بن كعب وإبراهيم النخعي: العذاب الأدنى مصائب الدنيا

QURTUBI-FULL:32:21/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:32:21/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:32:21/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas also identifies the lesser torment as the prescribed legal penalties.
QURTUBI-FULL:32:21/r2.anchor: وعنه أيضا أنه الحدود. وقال ابن مسعود والحسين بن علي وعبد الله بن الحارث

QURTUBI-FULL:32:21/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:32:21/r3.speaker: ابن مسعود والحسين بن علي وعبد الله بن الحارث
QURTUBI-FULL:32:21/r3.claim: Ibn Mas'ud, al-Husayn ibn Ali, and Abdullah ibn al-Harith say the lesser torment was being killed by the sword at Badr.
QURTUBI-FULL:32:21/r3.anchor: وقال ابن مسعود والحسين بن علي وعبد الله بن الحارث: هو القتل بالسيف يوم بدر

QURTUBI-FULL:32:21/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:32:21/r4.speaker: مقاتل ومجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:32:21/r4.claim: Maqatil and Mujahid identify it as the seven-year famine in Mecca, when people ate carrion.
QURTUBI-FULL:32:21/r4.anchor: وقال مقاتل: الجوع سبع سنين بمكة حتى أكلوا الجيف وقاله مجاهد

QURTUBI-FULL:32:21/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:32:21/r5.speaker: مجاهد والبراء بن عازب
QURTUBI-FULL:32:21/r5.claim: Mujahid and al-Bara ibn Azib are also cited for identifying the lesser torment as punishment in the grave.
QURTUBI-FULL:32:21/r5.anchor: وعنه أيضا: العذاب الأدنى عذاب القبر وقاله البراء بن عازب

QURTUBI-FULL:32:21/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:32:21/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:32:21/r6.claim: Qurtubi says the greater torment is generally agreed to be Hell, while reporting Ja'far ibn Muhammad's exception that it is the Mahdi's emergence with the sword; one report identifies the lesser torment as high prices.
QURTUBI-FULL:32:21/r6.anchor: ولا خلاف أن العذاب الأكبر عذاب جهنم إلا ما روي عن جعفر بن محمد أنه خروج المهدي بالسيف

QURTUBI-FULL:32:21/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:32:21/r7.speaker: القشيري
QURTUBI-FULL:32:21/r7.claim: Al-Qushayri reports an interpretation of the lesser torment as punishment in the grave but questions it because the verse says the torment may make them return.
QURTUBI-FULL:32:21/r7.anchor: قال القشيري: وقيل عذاب القبر. وفيه نظر لقوله: { لعلهم يرجعون }

QURTUBI-FULL:32:21/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:32:21/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:32:21/r8.claim: For those who understand the lesser torment as killing, “so that they may return” means those who survive may turn back.
QURTUBI-FULL:32:21/r8.anchor: ومن حمل العذاب على القتل قال: { لعلهم يرجعون } أي يرجع من بقي منهم

QURTUBI-FULL:32:21/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:32:21/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:32:21/r9.claim: For Mujahid's and al-Bara's view, the phrase can mean that people wish for and ask to return; the passive reading supports this, as does the usage that names an intended act as if performed.
QURTUBI-FULL:32:21/r9.anchor: وقد قيل: إن معنى قوله: { لعلهم يرجعون } على قول مجاهد والبراء: أي لعلهم يريدون الرجوع ويطلبونه
